entities.name: CCl4 liver injury
observations: Rat carbon tetrachloride hepatotoxicity models showed elevated liver enzymes, oxidative damage, antioxidant depletion, and histopathologic injury; this is the comparator condition for apitherapy interventions.

entities.name: Propolis
observations: In rat CCl4 injury, oral ethanolic propolis at 100–200 mg/kg improved transaminases, alkaline phosphatase, lipid peroxidation, glutathione depletion, and hepatocyte histology; 200 mg/kg post-treatment was described as most effective.

A Moroccan propolis study using 500 mg/kg orally for 12 days significantly improved CCl4-related liver-function and oxidative-stress abnormalities; numerical effect sizes were not available in the retrieved abstract.

entities.name: Royal jelly
observations: In CCl4-treated rats, royal jelly at 50–200 mg/kg reduced lipid peroxidation and liver enzymes, improved endogenous antioxidant defenses, and ameliorated histology versus CCl4 controls.

A later rat study reported movement of AST/ALT, lipid, oxidative-DNA, PON1, and liver-telomere outcomes toward control values; dose and numerical effect sizes were not available in the retrieved abstract.

entities.name: Bee pollen
observations: Chestnut bee pollen aqueous extract at 200 or 400 mg/kg/day for 7 days after CCl4 injury reversed AST/ALT, oxidative-stress, and histopathologic abnormalities; the abstract reported healing but no numerical magnitudes.

entities.name: Honey
observations: Carob honey at 2 g/kg significantly ameliorated CCl4-related liver enzymes, LDH, lipid/protein oxidation, and antioxidant depletion.

Sider honey improved hepato-renal and histopathologic parameters over four weeks, especially with Korean ginseng combination, but the design emphasized pretreatment and lacked numerical effect sizes in the retrieved abstract.

entities.name: Bee venom
observations: In a rat LPS-plus-CCl4 model, bee venom and honey reduced AST, ALT, alpha-fetoprotein, oxidative/hematologic abnormalities, and histopathology; the combination appeared more protective than either alone. Applicability to isolated CCl4 injury is limited.

entities.name: Apitherapy improves rat CCl4 injury
observations: Across small acute or subacute rat studies, propolis, royal jelly, bee pollen, honey, bee venom combinations, and mixed apitherapy diets generally improved liver biomarkers, oxidative stress, and/or histology versus CCl4 controls.

Evidence is positive for hepatoprotection or ameliorated recovery, but heterogeneous; several studies are prophylactic, numerical effect sizes are often unavailable, mixed products prevent attribution, and acceleration of true regeneration is not established.
